changes.before: Complete DeferredNote.store(_:) and read(). A new note reads "empty"; storing replaces the previous callback; read returns the current callback’s result. Keep @escaping where the closure parameter is stored.
changes.after: Save a closure now and call it later.

before: A closure escapes when it can outlive the call that receives it. Storing this nonoptional function parameter for later use needs @escaping. That annotation allows a longer lifetime; it does not run the callback in the background. Here store only saves the closure, and read calls it later, synchronously.

(() -> String)? is an optional no-input function returning text. DeferredNote() creates a value with action initially nil. mutating permits store to change this struct; self.action names the stored property, while action alone names the parameter. read uses if let to unwrap the saved function, then saved() invokes it. [label] is a capture list: it saves the current String value when the closure is created. Without that list, this example captures the variable and sees its later value. The earlier ARC lesson covers class-reference cycles; this value example is not a new memory-management guarantee.

Complete DeferredNote.store(_:) and read(). A new note reads "empty"; storing replaces the previous callback; read returns the current callback’s result. Keep @escaping where the closure parameter is stored. Optional local practice: choose one more input, predict the outcome, then run it. The checks observe the stated values and effects; they do not require one exact implementation spelling.
after: A closure is a function value. It escapes when it can remain available after the receiving function ends. @escaping allows this function parameter to be saved for later. It does not start background work.
(() -> String)? means an optional function that takes no inputs and returns text. DeferredNote starts with no saved function. store saves one; read calls it later or returns empty if none exists.

[label] is a capture list. Here it saves label's current String value when the closure is made. Changing label afterwards does not change that saved text. Without this capture list, this example's closure would read the variable's later value.
Complete store(_:) and read(). A new note returns empty. Saving a callback replaces the previous one. read must return the current callback's result, so call it when read runs.
Keep @escaping on the parameter that store saves. Without it, Swift rejects this assignment to a property. mutating is also needed because store changes a property of the struct.

before.question: With [label] capturing "open", label later becomes "closed". What does the stored callback return?
choices: The callback runs automatically when label changes
before.explanation: The capture list saves the String value at closure creation. Storing and calling are separate actions.

after.question: [label] saves the text open. label later becomes closed. What does this saved callback return?
choices: It runs by itself when label changes
after.explanation: The capture list saves the current String value, which was open.
